# LeakSanitizer suppressions.
#
# One entry, and it is a test's premise rather than a defect.
#
# `a_record_appended_past_the_digest_falls_back` asks what a *lazy* open does
# with a file whose writer put a record down and then died before flushing —
# the record is on disk, the digest at the end is stale, and the open must fall
# back to the scan. The only way to produce that file is a writer that never
# runs its `Drop`, because `Drop` is what flushes; the test does that with
# `std::mem::forget`. The 3502 bytes LeakSanitizer reports across six
# allocations are that forgotten writer's buffers, and a run that did not leak
# them would be a run that did not test anything. (Measured 2026-08-24 as
# `6  3502` on 0.7.0 and reported identically by CI on 0.8.0. This file said
# five allocations and 3494 bytes; when it stopped being that was not
# established, only that both measurements above disagree with it. Read the
# figure as "the whole of that test's leak" rather than as a threshold --
# nothing checks it, and it is expected to drift.)
#
# Scoped to the test function, deliberately. The leaking allocation's stack runs
# through `VarveFile::write_record_with_prev_key`, and suppressing *that* — the
# obvious frame to reach for — would blind the whole append path, which is the
# hottest allocating code in the library and exactly where a real leak would
# matter. Naming the test instead means any new leak anywhere, including one in
# `write_record_with_prev_key` reached from any other test, still fails the run.
#
# A name only matches a frame that has been *symbolized*, which makes this file
# useless without a symbolizer rather than merely less precise. On 2026-08-24 CI
# had none, every frame came out as a bare address, this entry matched nothing,
# and the job failed reporting the premise above as a leak. The ASan workflow
# now locates `llvm-symbolizer` in a step of its own and fails there when it
# cannot -- and note that rustup's `llvm-tools` component does not provide one.
leak:a_record_appended_past_the_digest_falls_back
